Apart from these two general classiﬁcations of carotenoids as cyclic or acyclic or carotenes and xanthophylls, other subgroups of
carotenoids can be distinguished by their structure. Some carotenoids have a 45- or 50-carbon skeleton, which are called higher
carotenoids. On the other hand, carotenoids composed of carbon skeletons with fewer than 40 carbons are called apocarotenoids.
Apocarotenoids correspond to products that are generated by oxidative cleavage of carotenoids, catalyzed by a family of enzymes
called carotenoid excision dioxygenases (Fernandes et al., 2018).
Finally, some of the carotenoids also act as precursors of vitamin A, allowing their classiﬁcation into provitamin A group (b-caro-
tene, a-carotene and b-cryptoxanthin) and non-provitamin A carotenoid group.
